Non lasciare mai aperta la porta non protetta del server su una rete di stabilimento: imposta Sicurezza su attivata, o su reciproca per verificare anche il certificato di questo nodo. La modalità finita esegue a ogni chiamata un'acquisizione dei campioni impostati. La modalità continua avvia l'attività alla prima chiamata e legge il blocco successivo di campioni a ogni chiamata seguente. y sono i campioni di un canale come array, o un array di array, uno per canale in ordine. dt sono i secondi tra i campioni. node.dia-filter.help: Un filtro di Butterworth: piatto nella banda che lascia passare, senza ondulazione, e 3 dB sotto alla frequenza di taglio. Passa-basso mantiene ciò che è più lento del taglio, passa-alto mantiene ciò che è più veloce, passa-banda mantiene ciò che sta tra i due bordi ed elimina-banda lo rimuove. Un ordine più alto taglia più nettamente e oscilla un po' più a lungo dopo un gradino. Il taglio deve essere sopra zero e sotto metà della frequenza di campionamento. Dagli un array, o un numero alla volta, e ricorda dov'era tra le chiamate di un'esecuzione, così un segnale tagliato a pezzi viene filtrato come uno solo. L'ingresso rate prevale sulla proprietà Campioni al secondo. Parte da fermo, quindi i primi campioni di un array portano un transitorio di avvio; ritarda il segnale di una quantità che dipende dalla frequenza, quindi è sbagliato usarlo dove la temporizzazione tra due segnali deve coincidere esattamente; e non è un filtro a fase lineare né a fase zero.

Un numero è memorizzato come float a 64 bit, un vero o falso come booleano e tutto il resto come testo. Una colonna che contiene un elenco di numeri li aggiunge tutti, ed è così che entra un blocco di campioni. Le proprietà vengono scritte nel file all'avvio dell'esecuzione. A un file già esistente si aggiunge in coda, così le esecuzioni si susseguono in un unico file, e un file troncato da un'interruzione di corrente viene riparato fino all'ultima riga completa prima di proseguire. Con la scrittura su disco attiva, un'interruzione di corrente perde al massimo la riga in scrittura. node.exec.compat: The three outputs, both buffered and streaming modes, the timeout and the appended message property all behave as Node-RED's do. Two things do not, and neither is negotiable. There is no shell: the command line is split on quoting rules only, and an unquoted shell metacharacter is refused rather than run, so one allowed command cannot become an arbitrary one. And the node is disabled until an operator names the commands a flow may run. Node-RED's exec node runs anything, and Node-RED starts with no authentication by default; a vendor shipping that default became CVE-2025-41656 (Pilz IndustrialPI 4, VDE-2025-045), unauthenticated command execution on the device. Output is capped per stream; a command that exceeds it is killed and reported rather than being allowed to fill the heap. A command that forks children of its own may leave them behind when it is killed.

node.function.compat: Runs on goja, a JavaScript interpreter written in Go, rather than Node's vm module. The language is ES2023; the Node standard library is not present. require() and npm modules do not work and cannot be made to without embedding Node. There is always a CPU time limit, which Node-RED leaves optional and off, and it applies to every timer callback too. setTimeout, setInterval and their clear functions work, on the node's clock, and every one is cleared when the flow stops or is redeployed. Buffer is there (alloc, from, concat, the read and write methods for integers and floats in both byte orders, slice, toString and toJSON). A byte slice in a message arrives as a byte array, so wrap it with Buffer.from.

node.http in.compat: Serves a path, with Express-style :params and a trailing *, and builds the same msg.req / msg.res / msg.payload shape Node-RED does, including JSON, form-encoded and raw bodies. Three deliberate differences. A request that no HTTP Response node answers is closed with 504 after a timeout instead of being held open forever, because Node-RED's version leaks a connection per request until the process runs out of sockets and stops answering with nothing in the log. Two nodes claiming the same method and path is refused at deploy time rather than one of them silently never firing. And a path that would shadow the editor or the admin API is refused for the same reason. Uploads parse the way multer does in Node-RED: text fields into msg.payload, files into msg.req.files, a broken upload answered with 500. One bound multer lacks: an array index over 10,000 in a field name, a[99999999], is refused instead of building a sparse array that long. msg.req.cookies is cookie-parser's, j: values included.

node.http request.compat: Method, URL, headers, basic authentication, redirects and the three return types, with msg.url, msg.method and msg.headers overriding the node. The response body is size-capped and the call is bounded by a timeout, neither of which Node-RED does. TLS comes from a tls-config, or without one msg.rejectUnauthorized = false skips the certificate check for that one message, as in Node-RED. msg.cookies and a cookie header go out through a cookie jar, cookies a redirect sets follow the redirect, and msg.responseCookies and msg.redirectList come back, all as in Node-RED. A multipart/form-data content type with an object payload sends it as a form. Proxy settings and connection persistence are not implemented in this build. There is no egress allowlist: this node can reach anything the pod can, exactly as Node-RED's can, and the place to bound that is a NetworkPolicy rather than an edit dialog nobody outside the cluster can trust. networkInterface (not in Node-RED) binds the connections to one network interface.

node.tcp in.compat: Listens or connects out, in stream mode with a delimiter or single mode collecting until the peer closes, with buffer, string or base64 payloads. Every message carries msg._session so a TCP Out node can reply on the same connection. Three bounds Node-RED does not have: the number of accepted connections, the size of one delimited message, and the total of a single-mode read. A peer that opens connections and never closes them, or sends without ever sending the delimiter, grows the heap until the pod dies otherwise. TLS through a tls-config works both ways: a listener presents the config's certificate, a client checks the server's.

node.tcp request.compat: Connects, sends the payload and waits for the reply, in any of Node-RED's four wait modes: a fixed time, a delimiter, a byte count, or until the peer closes. msg.host and msg.port override the node. Every request opens its own connection — Node-RED's connection-reuse mode is not implemented, and reusing one would change the semantics of the wait modes, which all end at a connection boundary. With a tls-config the server's certificate is checked unless the config says not to. It polls rather than using the kernel's notification interface, so a change is seen within the poll interval rather than immediately, and two changes inside one interval are reported once. node.xml.compat: Both directions, using xml2js's object convention: attributes under the key named by "attr" (default $), element text under "chr" (default _), and every child element as an array, which is xml2js's own explicitArray default. Set ew_explicitArray to false to collapse single children instead. The per-message msg.options that Node-RED passes through to xml2js is not honoured — the other xml2js options change the shape of the output, and silently ignoring one would produce an object the flow does not expect while looking like it worked. Namespaces are kept as part of the element name rather than being resolved.
